note.explanation: Photosynthesis is how plants, algae and some bacteria use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water. It happens in two phases: light reactions in the thylakoid membranes and dark reactions in the stroma. Chlorophyll absorbs light, and the light reactions make ATP and NADPH for the dark reactions.
examples: Light reactions release oxygen when light breaks water molecules.
In the dark reactions, carbon dioxide is used to make carbohydrates.
note.checkAnswer: Light reactions occur on the thylakoid membranes; dark reactions occur in the stroma.
note.simple: Plants use light to make food. The light reactions capture energy, and the dark reactions use that energy to make carbohydrates.
note.checkQuestion: Where do the light and dark reactions of photosynthesis take place?
note.title: Photosynthesis
steps: The light reactions use light energy to make ATP and NADPH and release oxygen from water.
The dark reactions use ATP and hydrogen from NADPH to reduce carbon dioxide and make carbohydrates.
The carbohydrates are used to make glucose.
note.answer: Photosynthesis is the synthesis of glucose from carbon dioxide and water in the presence of sunlight (and chlorophyll), with oxygen as a by-product.

mcqs.stem: Where do the light reactions of photosynthesis take place?
rationales: Correct: the light reactions take place on the thylakoid membranes of chloroplasts.
The stroma is where the dark reactions take place.
The section does not give the outer membrane as the site of light reactions.
The section places light reactions in chloroplast thylakoids, not the cytoplasm.

mcqs.stem: Which high-energy molecules are made during the light reactions?
rationales: Correct: the light reactions use light energy to make ATP and NADPH.
Glucose is made using products of the light reactions; oxygen is released as a by-product.
Carbon dioxide and water are raw materials, not the high-energy molecules made in the light reactions.
Proteins and lipids are not identified as products of the light reactions.

mcqs.stem: In which part of a chloroplast do the dark reactions take place?
rationales: Correct: the dark reactions take place in the stroma of chloroplasts.
The thylakoid membranes are the site of light reactions.
The cell wall is not the site of the dark reactions.
The nucleus is not the site of the dark reactions.

mcqs.stem: Which substance is broken by light during the light reactions, releasing oxygen?
rationales: Correct: light breaks water molecules, and oxygen is released.
Carbon dioxide is used in the dark reactions to make carbohydrates.
Glucose is made from carbohydrates produced during the dark reactions; it is not broken to release oxygen.
NADP is reduced to NADPH; it is not the molecule broken to release oxygen.

mcqs.stem: Which pigment is identified as the main pigment in the thylakoid membranes?
rationales: Correct: chlorophyll-a is the main pigment.
Chlorophyll-b is an accessory pigment.
Carotenoids are accessory pigments.
NADP is a coenzyme, not a pigment.

mcqs.stem: What do the 3-carbon compounds use to become 3-carbon carbohydrates in the dark reactions?
rationales: Correct: they are reduced using ATP and hydrogen from NADPH.
Oxygen and water are not the materials used for this reduction in the section's summary.
Glucose is made from the 3-carbon carbohydrates, and light is used in the light reactions.
These are pigments, not the materials used to reduce the 3-carbon compounds.

mcqs.stem: Which colours of light carry out more photosynthesis according to the section?
rationales: Correct: the section states that blue and red lights carry out more photosynthesis.
Green and yellow are not identified as the colours that carry out more photosynthesis.
The section says blue and red lights carry out more photosynthesis, not only green light.
The section does not identify only yellow light as carrying out more photosynthesis.

options: Accessory pigments absorb wavelengths not absorbed by chlorophyll-a.
Accessory pigments make carbon dioxide in the stroma.
Accessory pigments replace water as the raw material.
Accessory pigments convert glucose into light.
mcqs.stem: What is one role of accessory pigments in photosynthesis?
rationales: Correct: wavelengths not absorbed by chlorophyll-a are absorbed by accessory pigments.
The section does not state that accessory pigments make carbon dioxide.
Water remains a raw material in photosynthesis; pigments do not replace it.
The section says pigments absorb sunlight and convert it into chemical energy, not that they convert glucose into light.

written.text: Outline the processes involved in photosynthesis?
written.finalAnswer: Photosynthesis has light reactions and dark reactions. Light reactions occur on the thylakoid membranes and produce ATP and NADPH; they also release oxygen when light breaks water. Dark reactions occur in the stroma, where carbon dioxide is reduced using ATP and hydrogen from NADPH to make carbohydrates that are used to make glucose.

rubric.description: Names the dark reactions in the stroma and states that carbon dioxide is reduced.
rubric.how: Explain that carbon dioxide is reduced in the stroma.

rubric.why: The outline must state the food product made through the process.
rubric.description: States that the carbohydrates are used to make glucose.
rubric.how: Finish by naming glucose as the product made from the carbohydrates.

modelAnswer: Photosynthesis occurs in two phases: light reactions and dark reactions.

explain.title: What photosynthesis means
explain.body: Your textbook defines photosynthesis as: “Photosynthesis is the synthesis of glucose from carbon dioxide and water in the presence of sunlight (and chlorophyll), with oxygen as a by-product.” In simple terms, organisms use light to make food from raw materials.

explain.title: The two phases
explain.body: Photosynthesis has light reactions and dark reactions. Light reactions take place on the thylakoid membranes of chloroplasts. Dark reactions take place in the stroma of the chloroplasts.

explain.title: What happens in the light reactions
explain.body: Chlorophyll absorbs light and releases high-energy electrons. Their energy helps produce ATP. Light also breaks water, releasing oxygen. Electrons and hydrogen ions are used to reduce NADP to NADPH.

explain.title: What happens in the dark reactions
explain.body: Carbon dioxide combines with 5-carbon compounds. The resulting unstable 6-carbon compounds split into 3-carbon compounds. ATP and hydrogen from NADPH help make 3-carbon carbohydrates, which are used to make glucose and regenerate the 5-carbon compounds.

explain.title: Pigments absorb light
explain.body: Your textbook defines pigments as: “Pigments are the substances that absorb visible light. Different pigments absorb light of different wavelengths (colours).” Chlorophyll-a is the main pigment; chlorophyll-b and carotenoids are accessory pigments.

mistakes: Do not swap the locations: light reactions take place on thylakoid membranes; dark reactions take place in the stroma.
Do not say oxygen comes from carbon dioxide; light breaks water and oxygen is released.
Do not confuse chlorophyll-a with the accessory pigments. Chlorophyll-a is the main pigment.
Do not leave NADPH out when describing the light reactions; it is used with ATP in the dark reactions.
When writing the word equation, include light energy and all the products shown in your textbook.
